title: The destructor must be virtual too
description:
`Loud` holds something that must be released in its destructor (here it just adjusts a counter). The test creates a `Loud` on the heap and deletes it **through a pointer to the base class**.

As written, only `Quiet`'s destructor runs, `Loud`'s is skipped, and the counter never comes back down. That is undefined behaviour and, in real code, a leak.

Fix it with one word in the base class.
unitTests:
static_assert(std::has_virtual_destructor_v<Quiet>, "a class with virtual functions needs a virtual destructor");
TEST("deleting through a base pointer runs the derived destructor") { g_resources = 0; Quiet* p{ new Loud{} }; CHECK_EQ(g_resources, 1); CHECK_EQ(p->volume(), 11); delete p; CHECK_EQ(g_resources, 0); }

grading.unitTests:
